deep.reconstruction:
This folio is the last page of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation', dated 14 January 1847 and printed posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke (1876). The page holds no derivation, only the end of the closing sentence begun on folio 30 (p. 30).

The full sentence reads: 'Schliesslich bemerken wir noch, dass sich die aufgestellte Theorie mit derselben Sicherheit auch auf den Fall ausdehnen lässt, wo man den in Rede stehenden Grössen imaginäre Werthe beilegt.' In English: 'Finally we remark that the theory set up can be extended with the same certainty to the case where one assigns imaginary values to the quantities in question.'

This claims, without proof, that the whole theory of the operator d^nu/dx^nu extends to complex values. That means complex order nu and presumably complex argument x and the parameters of the examples, such as the exponent mu in x^mu.

The tools developed on the earlier pages would support this:
- The integral representation d^nu f(x) = 1/Pi(-nu-1) * Integral_k^x f(t)(x-t)^(-nu-1) dt, with Pi(s) = Gamma(s+1), valid for Re(nu) < 0.
- The series and analytic continuation that give formulas 12-14.
- These formulas involve Pi and Psi = d log Pi / ds, which are analytic in nu. Formulas such as 13, d^nu e^x = e^x, and 14 therefore continue analytically to complex nu.

The author's place-and-date line 'Göttingen den 14. Jan. 1847' and the initials (apparently 'B. R.') are struck through. The archive foliation is '31.' (top right) and '17' (right margin).

Context from the previous page, for checking:
- Formula 13 uses the substitution y = x - t: Integral_{-inf}^x e^t (x-t)^(-nu-1) dt = e^x Gamma(-nu) = e^x Pi(-nu-1). This gives d^nu e^x = e^x, valid for Re(nu) < 0 and then extended.
- Formula 14 obtains d^nu log x from d^(nu-1) x^(-1).
errors: No mathematical content on this page to err. The claim of extension to imaginary values is asserted without justification. It is plausible via analytic continuation in nu, but convergence conditions (e.g. Re(nu)<0 for the integral representation) are not discussed.

Context note (previous page, formula 14): the modern Riemann–Liouville result with base point 0 is D^nu log x = x^(-nu)/Gamma(1-nu) * (log x - gamma - psi(1-nu)). Riemann's form uses Psi(s) = psi(s+1), so Psi(-nu) - Psi(0) = psi(1-nu) - psi(1). As transcribed with a '+' sign, it gives x log x + x for nu = -1 instead of x log x - x. Either the sign in the transcription or Riemann's normalisation of complementary terms should be checked against the image of folio 30.

results.what: Remark that the theory of differentiation/integration of arbitrary order extends to imaginary (complex) values of the quantities involved, in particular the order nu.
results.modern_name: Fractional calculus of complex order (Riemann–Liouville operators with complex nu, via analytic continuation)
results.usually_credited_to: Liouville (1832ff.) considered general orders; complex-order Riemann–Liouville integrals were developed systematically later (e.g. Holmgren 1865-67, Marcel Riesz 1949, Hadamard finite parts).

deep.surprise_reason: This is the closing sentence and struck-out date line of Riemann's 1847 essay on fractional integration and differentiation. The essay was published in his Werke (1876) and is the origin of the 'Riemann' in Riemann–Liouville. The remark about imaginary values appears in the published text. Nothing new.

checkable.asserts: The integral in formula 13 equals Gamma(-nu) = Pi(-nu-1), so d^nu e^x = e^x (for Re(nu)<0).

The modern formula D^nu log x = x^(-nu)/Gamma(1-nu)(log x - gamma - psi(1-nu)) at nu=-1 gives the antiderivative x log x - x (zero difference). This checks the sign convention of formula 14 on the previous page.
At nu=-1 (so the operator is d^(nu-1) applied to x^(-1)), with lower limit 1, the antiderivative of 1/t is log x. This is consistent with formula 14 as d^nu log x = d^(nu-1) x^(-1).

transcription_corrections: 'ausdehnen[?] sucht' should read 'ausdehnen lässt' (läßt). This completes 'dass sich die aufgestellte Theorie ... auch auf den Fall ausdehnen lässt'.
'in Rede stehenden' is correct. 'Grössen' is written with ß ('Größen'). 'imaginäre Werthe beilegt' is correct (word split 'Wer-/the').
Struck-out date line reads 'Göttingen den 14. Jan.' and '1847'. The struck initials appear to be 'B. R.'.
Archive marks: '31.' at top right (page number continuing from 30) and folio number '17' in the right margin.
